section.content: 为克服现有技术中锂电池的电芯强度低、电池易出现扭曲变形的技术问题，本申请提供一种水性粘结剂及改性隔膜和电池；水性粘结剂是具有核壳结构的粘结剂颗粒，所述核壳结构的粘结剂颗粒中核是聚合物A，壳是聚合物B；所述核的玻璃化转变温度为80℃～150℃；所述壳的玻璃化转变温度为30℃～70℃。本申请提供的核壳结构的粘结剂颗粒，涂覆于隔膜基材表面，制备得到的电芯经过热压后，隔膜与正负极片粘结成一体，使得电池具有更高的强度，电池的抗扭曲变形性好，同时提升隔膜的透气性，降低电池生产成本，适用于生产薄型电池，并保持好的电池性能。

In order to solve the technical problems of low cell strength and easy distortion of the battery of the lithium battery in the prior art, the application provides an aqueous binder, a modified diaphragm and the battery; the water-based binder is a binder particle with a core-shell structure, wherein the core of the binder particle with the core-shell structure is a polymer A, and the shell is a polymer B; the glass transition temperature of the core is 80-150 ℃; the glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃. The core-shell structured adhesive particles provided by the application are coated on the surface of the diaphragm substrate, and the prepared battery core is bonded with the positive and negative plates into a whole after hot pressing, so that the battery has higher strength, good anti-buckling deformability, improved air permeability of the diaphragm, reduced production cost of the battery, suitability for producing thin batteries and good battery performance.

Aqueous binder, modified diaphragm, battery and preparation method of aqueous binder

Technical Field

The application belongs to the technical field of lithium battery preparation, and particularly relates to a water-based binder, a modified diaphragm, a battery and a preparation method of the water-based binder.

Background

The lithium battery has the advantages of long cycle life, wide use temperature range, high energy density and power density, no memory effect and the like, is widely applied to 3C products such as personal computers, mobile phones and the like, and becomes the best choice of power sources of electric automobiles. With the continuous increase of the development demands of terminal equipment, lithium batteries tend to be large-sized and thin, and on one hand, batteries are required to have higher energy density, long cycle life and safety, and on the other hand, batteries are required to be thinner and thinner, and the batteries themselves have certain strength. The strength of the traditional lithium battery is obviously weakened along with the thickness reduction; particularly, the large-area battery has poor hardness, is easy to distort and deform, influences the application of devices, and even has great influence on the performance and the safety of the battery. The reason for the poor strength is that in the conventional battery, the battery composition is a stack combination of the positive electrode, the separator and the negative electrode in sequence, and the electrolyte is injected into the stack combination, so that the positive electrode and the separator, the separator and the negative electrode slide relatively due to the smooth surface of the separator and the lubrication effect after the electrolyte is added, and the positive electrode and the negative electrode sheet are sheets with the thickness of about hundreds of micrometers and formed by metal foil and inorganic powder, and have insufficient strength. The battery can only depend on the pole piece physical superposition supporting strength of about hundreds of micrometers, and the relative displacement is arranged between the layers, so that the battery strength cannot meet the requirements of device application in the practical application process, in addition, the battery is distorted after the area of the battery is increased, the electric performance and the safety of the battery are affected, and even the battery burns and explodes.

In order to solve the problems, the current industry adopts a solution that an aqueous or oily PVDF polymer is used for coating a polyolefin diaphragm/a ceramic coating diaphragm, and a pole piece and the diaphragm are compounded together through hot pressing so as to provide enough battery hardness and prevent distortion. Under the continuous expansion of application requirements in the fields of lithium battery manufacturing, photovoltaic backboard, energy storage and the like, PVDF shows explosive growth, and R142b serving as a main production raw material of a fluoride engineering product PVDF can only be produced in a quota due to the fact that the atmosphere is damaged and limited by international agreements, so that the risk of supply shortage exists.

Disclosure of Invention

Aiming at the technical problems of low cell strength and easy distortion of the battery of the lithium battery in the prior art, the application provides a water-based adhesive, a modified diaphragm, the battery and a preparation method of the water-based adhesive.

In order to solve the technical problems, the application provides an aqueous binder, which comprises binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the core of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer A, and the shell is a polymer B;

the glass transition temperature of the core is 80-150 ℃;

the glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃.

Preferably, the particle size of the binder particles is in the range of 1 to 10 μm; the particle size of the core is in the range of 0.5 to 4 μm.

Preferably, the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1, based on 100% of the mass of the binder particles of one core-shell structure: (0.2-10).

Preferably, the reactants for preparing the polymer A comprise a polymerization monomer a1, a cross-linking agent a2, a dispersing agent a3 and an initiator a4;

based on 100% of the mass of the polymerization monomer a1, the mass ratio of the cross-linking agent a2 is 4-30%, the mass ratio of the dispersing agent a3 is 0.1-25%, and the mass ratio of the initiator a4 is 0.3-5%.

Preferably, the polymerization monomer a1 comprises one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylic acid esters and styrene;

the cross-linking agent a2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate;

the dispersing agent a3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG);

the initiator a4 comprises one or more of persulfates, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, dibenzoyl peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide.

Preferably, the reactants for preparing the polymer B comprise a polymerization reaction monomer B1, a cross-linking agent B2, a dispersing agent B3 and an initiator B4, and are prepared by dispersion polymerization;

the mass ratio of the cross-linking agent b2 is 1-20 percent, the mass ratio of the dispersing agent b3 is 0-10 percent, and the mass ratio of the initiator b4 is 0.5-5 percent based on 100 percent of the mass ratio of the polymerization monomer b 1.

Preferably, the polymerization monomer b1 comprises one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylic acid esters and styrene;

the cross-linking agent b2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate;

the dispersing agent b3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG);

the initiator b4 comprises one or more of persulfates, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, benzoyl Peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide.

In another aspect, the present application provides a method for preparing an aqueous binder, comprising the steps of:

(1) Preparation of the core solution: adding a solvent and an initiator a4 into a reaction kettle, uniformly stirring, then adding a polymerization reaction monomer a1 and a cross-linking agent a2, stirring, introducing a protective atmosphere, adding a dispersing agent a3, heating to react at 50-90 ℃ for 4-24 h, and preparing a nuclear solution after the reaction is finished; the mass ratio of the polymerization monomer a1 to the solvent is 10% -45%;

(2) Preparation of core-shell structure binder: mixing the core solution with the polymer B, or mixing the core solution with reactants for preparing the polymer B, heating to react at 50-90 ℃ for 4-24 hours, and preparing the core-shell structured binder after the reaction is finished;

the solvent comprises one or more of water and alcohol compounds.

In another aspect, the application provides a modified membrane, comprising a coating and a membrane substrate, wherein the coating is formed by coating the aqueous binder on the surface of the membrane substrate and drying.

On the other hand, the application provides a lithium battery, which comprises a positive plate, a negative plate and a diaphragm which is arranged between the adjacent positive plate and negative plate, wherein the diaphragm is the modified diaphragm.

The beneficial effects are that:

the aqueous binder provided by the application comprises binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the glass transition temperature of the core is 80-150 ℃, and after the prepared battery core is subjected to a hot pressing process, the core keeps the original shape, does not block diaphragm holes, and improves the air permeability of the diaphragm; the glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃, and the adhesive force between the electrode plate and the diaphragm can be improved in the hot pressing process of the battery cell prepared by the diaphragm and the electrode plate; the core-shell structured adhesive particles provided by the application are coated on the surface of the diaphragm substrate, and the prepared battery core is bonded with the positive and negative plates into a whole after hot pressing, so that the battery has higher strength, good anti-buckling deformability, improved air permeability of the diaphragm, reduced production cost of the battery, suitability for producing thin batteries and good battery performance. The aqueous binder provided by the application is environment-friendly and accords with the green sustainable development road.

Detailed Description

In order to make the technical problems, technical schemes and beneficial effects solved by the application more clear, the application is further described in detail below with reference to the embodiments. It should be understood that the specific embodiments described herein are for purposes of illustration only and are not intended to limit the scope of the application.

The application provides an aqueous binder, which comprises binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the core of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer A, and the shell is a polymer B. The core has a glass transition temperature of 80 ℃ to 150 ℃ and the shell has a glass transition temperature of 30 ℃ to 70 ℃.

The inventor finds through a large number of experiments that the battery core prepared by the diaphragm and the pole piece in the lithium battery needs to be subjected to a hot pressing process, if the glass transition temperature of the core of the binder particles is lower than 80 ℃, the core deforms and takes a flat shape, and the deformed core with a certain thickness easily blocks the diaphragm hole, so that the ventilation value of the diaphragm is reduced, and the electrical property of the battery is influenced. The glass transition temperature of the core in the adhesive particle prepared by the application is 80-150 ℃, the core is not deformed and does not block the diaphragm hole after the hot pressing process is carried out on the battery core, so that the diaphragm has higher ventilation value, the ventilation of the diaphragm is improved, and the prepared battery has better electric performance.

The glass transition temperature of the shell is in the range of 30-70 ℃, the bonding force between the pole piece and the diaphragm can be improved, the hardness of the battery is improved, the diaphragm layers of the coiled diaphragm have proper bonding force, the diaphragm is easy to tear in the unreeling and using process, and the yield of the diaphragm is improved. If the glass transition temperature of the shell is lower than 30 ℃, the diaphragms between the diaphragm layers are bonded with the diaphragms when the diaphragms are rolled after being coated in the preparation process of the diaphragms, the diaphragms are not easy to tear in the unreeling use process, and the yield of the diaphragms is reduced. If the glass transition temperature of the shell is higher than 70 ℃, the hardness of the shell is increased, the bonding force between the electrode plate and the diaphragm is reduced in the hot pressing process of the battery core prepared from the diaphragm and the electrode plate, the electrode plate and the diaphragm relatively slide after liquid injection, and the hardness of the battery is reduced. The glass transition temperature of the shell is in the range of 30 to 70 ℃, for example, the glass transition temperature of the shell may be 30 ℃, 35 ℃, 40 ℃,45 ℃, 50 ℃, 55 ℃, 60 ℃, 65 ℃, 70 ℃ or the like.

The aqueous binder provided by the application comprises binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the glass transition temperature of the core is 80-150 ℃, and the prepared battery core maintains the original shape after the hot pressing process, does not block diaphragm holes, and improves the air permeability of the diaphragm. The glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃, and the adhesive force between the electrode plate and the diaphragm can be improved in the hot pressing process of the battery cell prepared by the diaphragm and the electrode plate. The core-shell structured binder particles provided by the application are coated on the surface of the membrane substrate, and the prepared battery core is bonded with the positive and negative plates into a whole after hot pressing, so that the battery has higher strength, good anti-buckling deformability, and meanwhile, the air permeability of the membrane is improved, the production cost of the battery is reduced, and the good battery performance is maintained. The adhesive particles with the core-shell structure provided by the application can strengthen the adhesion between the diaphragm and the pole piece, and are more suitable for producing thin batteries, so that the batteries have higher strength, and are also suitable for batteries with medium thickness or thicker thickness.

In some embodiments, the binder particles have a particle size in the range of 1 to 10 μm and the cores have a particle size in the range of 0.5 to 4 μm. Preferably, the particle size of the binder particles is 2 to 5. Mu.m, and the particle size of the core is 0.5 to 4. Mu.m.

Specifically, the binder particles with the core-shell structure are mainly obtained by polymerization in a dispersion polymerization mode, the difference is that the particle size of emulsion polymerization is generally not more than 1 mu m from the existing emulsion polymerization mode, the binder particles provided by the application are obtained by adopting the dispersion polymerization mode, the particle size of the binder can be between 1 and 10 mu m, and the particle size of the core is between 0.5 and 4 mu m. The adhesive particles with large particle size can increase the friction force between the diaphragm and the pole piece and improve the adhesive force between the diaphragm and the pole piece. For example, the particle size of the binder particles may be 1 μm, 2 μm, 3 μm, 4 μm, 5 μm, 6 μm, 7 μm, 8 μm, 9 μm, 10 μm. The particle diameter of the core is 0.5-4 mu m, and the probability of blocking the diaphragm holes can be reduced and the air permeability of the diaphragm can be improved in the coating process of the core with large particle diameter. The particle diameter of the core may be, for example, 0.5 μm, 1.0 μm, 1.5 μm, 2.0 μm, 2.5 μm, 3.0 μm, 4.0 μm.

In some embodiments, the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1, based on 100% of the mass of the binder particles of one core-shell structure: (0.2-10).

In the adhesive particle with the core-shell structure, the core and the shell occupy a certain mass, and the mass ratio of the core to the shell in the adhesive particle with the core-shell structure provided by the application is 1: (0.2-10), and the particle diameter of the binder particles is in the range of 1-10 μm, the particle diameter of the core is in the range of 0.5-4 μm, and the shell is easy to completely contain the polymer A particles inside to form a core-shell structure; the prepared adhesive particles are coated on the surface of the diaphragm, the diaphragm has better air permeability, the adhesive force between the diaphragm and the pole piece is higher, the battery has higher strength, and the high-temperature expansion rate of the battery is lower. If the mass ratio of the core to the shell is lower than 1:0.2, namely the particle size of the shell is small, the shell cannot better coat the core, a core-shell structure cannot be formed, and sufficient peeling strength cannot be provided after hot pressing. If the mass ratio of the core to the shell is higher than 1:10, the particle size of the shell is too large, and the particle size of the core is too small, the adhesive cannot provide effective support, and under hot pressing, the adhesive is easy to deform and block holes, so that the air permeability is poor.

In some embodiments, preparing the polymer a includes polymerizing a polymerization monomer a1, a cross-linking agent a2, a dispersing agent a3, and an initiator a4 by dispersion polymerization;

based on 100 mass percent of the polymerization monomer a1, the mass percent of the cross-linking agent a2 is 4-30%, the mass percent of the dispersing agent a3 is 0.1-25%, and the mass percent of the initiator a4 is 0.3-5%.

In some preferred embodiments, the polymerization monomer a1 comprises one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylates, styrene; the acrylic acid esters include butyl acrylate, methyl acrylate, ethyl acrylate, methyl methacrylate, isooctyl acrylate, etc.; these polymerization monomers may be used alone, or two or more kinds may be used in combination, and may be selected according to the need. The cross-linking agent a2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate; these crosslinking agents may be used alone or in combination. The dispersing agent a3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG); the nonionic surfactant may be sodium dodecyl sulfate, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-9, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-15, etc., and the nonionic surfactant may be obtained by purchase. Polyvinylpyrrolidone may be selected from PVP-K30, K60 or K90, and may be obtained commercially. The initiator a4 comprises one or more of persulfates, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, dibenzoyl peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide; the persulfate may be sodium persulfate, potassium persulfate, ammonium persulfate, or the like.

In some embodiments, preparing the polymer B includes polymerizing a polymerization monomer B1, a cross-linking agent B2, a dispersing agent B3, and an initiator B4 by dispersion polymerization;

based on 100 mass percent of the polymerization monomer b1, the mass percent of the cross-linking agent b2 is 1-20%, the mass percent of the dispersing agent b3 is 0-10%, and the mass percent of the initiator b4 is 0.5-5%.

In some preferred embodiments, the polymerization monomer b1 includes one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylates, styrene; the acrylic acid esters include butyl acrylate, methyl acrylate, ethyl acrylate, methyl methacrylate, isooctyl acrylate, etc.; these polymerization monomers may be used alone, or two or more kinds may be used in combination, and may be selected according to the need.

The cross-linking agent b2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate; these crosslinking agents may be used alone or in combination.

The dispersing agent b3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG); the nonionic surfactant may be sodium dodecyl sulfate, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-9, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-15, etc., and the nonionic surfactant may be obtained by purchase.

The initiator b4 comprises one or more of persulfates, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, benzoyl Peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide; the persulfate may be sodium persulfate, potassium persulfate, ammonium persulfate, or the like.

In another aspect, the present application provides a method of preparing an aqueous binder comprising the steps of:

(1) Preparation of the core solution: adding a solvent and an initiator a4 into a reaction kettle, uniformly stirring, then adding a polymerization reaction monomer a1 and a cross-linking agent a2, stirring, introducing a protective atmosphere, adding a dispersing agent a3, heating to react at 50-90 ℃ for 4-4 h, and preparing a nuclear solution after the reaction is finished; the mass ratio of the polymerization monomer a1 to the solvent is 10% -45%;

(2) Preparation of core-shell structure binder: mixing the core solution with the polymer B, or mixing the core solution with reactants for preparing the polymer B, heating to react at 50-90 ℃ for 4-24 hours, and preparing the core-shell structured binder after the reaction is finished;

the solvent comprises one or more of water and alcohol compounds.

The alcohol compound comprises unit alcohol such as methanol, ethanol, propanol, isobutanol, n-butanol, isopropanol, amyl alcohol, and the like, and can also comprise polyalcohol such as propylene glycol, butanediol, glycerol, and the like.

The protective atmosphere comprises nitrogen and inert gases, and the inert gases comprise helium, neon, argon and the like.

Specifically, the preparation of the core-shell structure binder comprises two methods, namely, a first method: adding a reactant of the polymer B into a core solution, then carrying out a heating reaction, and preparing a core-shell structured binder after the reaction is finished; the second method is as follows: stirring the reactant of the polymer B, mixing with the core solution, and carrying out a heating reaction to obtain the core-shell structured binder after the reaction is finished. The preparation steps of the first and second methods are specifically described below.

The method comprises the following steps: and adding a polymerization monomer b1, a cross-linking agent b2 and a dispersing agent b3 into the core solution, uniformly stirring, adding an initiator b4, and heating to react to obtain the core-shell structured binder.

The second method is as follows: adding solvent water, a polymerization monomer b1, a cross-linking agent b2, a dispersing agent b3 and an initiator b4 into a reaction kettle, uniformly stirring, adding the core solution, uniformly mixing, and heating for reaction to obtain the binder with the core-shell structure.

In another aspect, the application provides a modified membrane, comprising a coating and a membrane substrate, wherein the coating is formed by coating the aqueous binder on the surface of the membrane substrate and drying.

Specifically, the modified diaphragm can be prepared by directly coating an aqueous binder on the surface of a diaphragm substrate and drying the aqueous binder; the ceramic particles and the aqueous binder are uniformly mixed and then coated on the surface of the diaphragm substrate, and the diaphragm substrate is dried to form the diaphragm. The ceramic particles include aluminum oxide, silicon dioxide, zirconium oxide, titanium oxide, calcium oxide, magnesium oxide, etc., preferably aluminum oxide; or the aqueous binder is coated on the surface of the ceramic diaphragm substrate and dried to form the modified diaphragm.

On the other hand, the application also provides a lithium battery, which comprises a positive plate, a negative plate and a diaphragm which is arranged between the adjacent positive plate and negative plate, wherein the diaphragm is the modified diaphragm.

In some embodiments, the positive electrode further comprises a positive electrode current collector, and the positive electrode material layer covers the surface of the positive electrode current collector.

The positive current collector comprises one or more of Al, ni, tin and copper, and the positive current collector is preferably selected from aluminum foil; the positive electrode active material layer further comprises a positive electrode binder and a positive electrode conductive agent, and the positive electrode active material, the positive electrode binder and the positive electrode conductive agent are blended to obtain the positive electrode material layer.

The positive electrode active material includes lithium cobaltate, lithium iron phosphate, lithium carbonate, and the like; the binder comprises polyvinylidene fluoride, styrene butadiene rubber and copolymer of vinylidene fluoride; the conductive agent comprises one or more of conductive carbon black, conductive carbon spheres, conductive graphite, conductive carbon fibers, carbon nanotubes, graphene or reduced graphene oxide.

The negative electrode further comprises a negative electrode current collector, and the negative electrode material layer covers the surface of the negative electrode current collector. The material of the negative electrode current collector may be the same as that of the positive electrode current collector, and will not be described again. In a more preferred embodiment, the negative current collector is selected from copper foil. The negative electrode material layer comprises a negative electrode active material, wherein the negative electrode active material comprises graphite, hard carbon, soft carbon, graphene, mesophase carbon microspheres and the like; the negative electrode material layer further comprises a negative electrode binder and a negative electrode conductive agent, and the negative electrode active material, the negative electrode binder and the negative electrode conductive agent are blended to obtain the negative electrode material layer. The negative electrode binder and the negative electrode conductive agent may be the same as the positive electrode binder and the positive electrode conductive agent, respectively, and will not be described again here.

In some embodiments, the separator substrate may be an existing conventional separator including single layer PP (polypropylene), single layer PE (polyethylene), double layer PP/PE, double layer PP/PP, and triple layer PP/PE/PP etc. separators.

The application is further illustrated by the following examples.

Example 1

1) Preparation of the core solution:

1200g of water and 0.4g of sodium dodecyl sulfate are added into a glass reaction kettle, 300g of methyl methacrylate and 45g of divinylbenzene are added after uniform stirring, nitrogen is added for 30min, 1.0g of ammonium persulfate is added, the temperature is raised to 80 ℃ for reaction for 10h, after the reaction is finished, the reaction kettle is cooled to room temperature, a nuclear solution is obtained, and the particle size of the obtained nuclear is tested to be 0.75 mu m. The glass transition temperature of the test core was 125 ℃.

2) Preparation of core-shell structure binder:

800g of water, 32g of sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), 10g of secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-9, 200g of butyl acrylate, 467g of acrylonitrile, 20g of diallyl phthalate and 10g of AIBN are added into a reaction kettle, after being uniformly dispersed at a high speed, 438g of the prepared core solution is added, stirring is carried out for 16 hours at room temperature, then the temperature is increased to 80 ℃, the reaction is carried out for 8 hours at the temperature of 80 ℃ to obtain a white binder with a core-shell structure, wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:7 the particle size of the test binder was 1.5. Mu.m. The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured by DSC to be 62 ℃.

Example 2

1) Preparation of the core solution:

450g of water, 450g of isopropanol, 25g of PVP-K30 and 15g of secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-15 are added into a glass reaction kettle, 300g of styrene and 30g of diallyl phthalate are added after uniform stirring, stirring is carried out for 30min, 10g of dibenzoyl peroxide is added, the temperature is raised to 80 ℃, the reaction is carried out for 10h under the condition of 80 ℃, after the reaction is finished, the reaction is cooled to room temperature, a nuclear solution is obtained, and the particle size of the obtained nuclear is tested to be 1.8 mu m. The glass transition temperature of the test core was 107 ℃.

2) Preparation of core-shell structure binder:

adding 112g of isooctyl acrylate, 208g of methyl methacrylate and 9.6g of trimethylolpropane triacrylate into the calculated amount of the core solution, stirring for 3 hours, adding 10g of dibenzoyl peroxide, heating to 80 ℃, and reacting for 8 hours at 80 ℃ to obtain a white binder with a core-shell structure, wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:1.68, the particle size of the test binder was 2.5. Mu.m. The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured by DSC to be 30 ℃.

Example 3

1) Preparation of the core solution:

900g of water, 20g of PEG-2000 are added into a glass reaction kettle, 300g of styrene, 15g of divinylbenzene and 30g of butyl acrylate are added after uniform stirring, nitrogen is stirred and introduced for 30min, 5g of dimethyl azodiisobutyrate is added, the temperature is raised to 78 ℃, the reaction is carried out for 8 hours at 78 ℃, after the reaction is finished, the reaction is cooled to room temperature, a nuclear solution is obtained, and the particle size of the obtained nuclear is tested to be 4.0 mu m. The glass transition temperature of the test core was 84 ℃.

2) Preparation of core-shell structure binder:

64g of butyl acrylate, 256g of acrylonitrile and 5g of N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide are added into the core solution, after stirring for 3 hours, 5g of dimethyl azodiisobutyrate is added, the temperature is raised to 80 ℃, and the reaction is carried out for 8 hours at 80 ℃ to obtain a white binder with a core-shell structure, wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:0.95, the particle size of the test binder was 5.0. Mu.m. The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured by DSC to be 70 ℃.

Example 4

This example is for illustrating the preparation method of the aqueous binder disclosed in the present application, and includes most of the steps of example 1, which are different in that: the particle diameter of the core was 4.0 μm and the glass transition temperature of the core was 130 ℃; wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:2.9 the particle size of the test binder was 6.3 μm and the glass transition temperature of the shell was 30℃using DSC.

Example 5

This example is for illustrating the preparation method of the aqueous binder disclosed in the present application, and includes most of the steps of example 1, which are different in that: the particle diameter of the core was 4.0 μm and the glass transition temperature of the core was 145 ℃; wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:0.95, the particle size of the test binder was 5.0 μm and the glass transition temperature of the shell was 63℃using DSC.

Example 6

This example is for illustrating the preparation method of the aqueous binder disclosed in the present application, and includes most of the steps of example 2, which are different in that: the particle diameter of the core is 1.8 μm, and the glass transition temperature of the core is 107 ℃; wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:36, the particle size of the test binder was 6.0 μm. The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured by DSC to be 40 ℃.

Comparative example 2
